task: fresh-context stratified capability-vs-style and ecosystem audit

items.proposed_content: The essential transferable data are invariant spectral structure plus arithmetic commuting operators, not holomorphicity itself.
Evidence should be evaluated by the quantifier and mechanism it supports, not by surface similarity to the target conclusion.

The construction separates a universal interface—local parameters, completion, and duality—from the additional analytic realization required to prove that the interface defines a global meromorphic function.

Across the source's L-function survey, direct analytic control weakens when an object is specified chiefly by increasingly general local Euler data. Continuation and functional equations are recovered when a second realization is available--through class-field or character-theoretic reduction, modular transformation plus Hecke eigenstructure, or automorphic spectral data--while the Selberg class packages the recurring outputs without explaining their origin.

The cited sections separately audit why several evidence types do not entail total zero control, diagnose a coupled analytic-arithmetic difficulty, and conjecture ingredients for a future proof, but they do not establish that the proxy failures are caused by that coupled bottleneck.

The source locates a qualitative boundary between rational or finitely coded zeta functions and global arithmetic Euler products. Finite-field cohomology and finite symbolic coding compress infinitely many counts into finitely controlled polynomials or matrices, but assembling local factors across rationally independent prime frequencies produces a nonperiodic transcendental object whose continuation and divisor require new global input.

The source develops a common divisor-frequency architecture in stages: logarithmic differentiation puts prime powers and reciprocals of zeros in one coordinate system; Mellin-Fourier inversion converts that identity into prime-counting formulas; and Poisson-Newton abstracts both sides as distributions, with prime-power frequencies and the meromorphic divisor as dual data.

The source uses divisor-frequency transform structure to explain why explicit formulas, spectral trace formulas, random-matrix statistics, and semiclassical orbit sums can resemble one another without selecting a literal Hilbert-Polya spectrum. The finite-state dynamical example sharpens the contrast: there a concrete transition matrix really does turn orbit counts into traces and a determinant, whereas no comparable canonical operator is constructed for Riemann zeta.

The source moves from reported cross-zero repulsion patterns to an algebraic proposal: root multiplication on rational local factors defines the ene-product, its primewise lift predicts additive convolution of global divisors, and the resulting character-product rule organizes the observed deficit locations. A unit equation then suggests an RH obstruction, but only heuristically.

The source compares two kinds of rigidity for analytic interpolation from arithmetic samples. In the archimedean setting, Gamma and related zeta data require low growth and symmetry or convexity in addition to their discrete values; in the p-adic setting, Kummer congruences, residue-class branches, and removal of the local Euler factor make Bernoulli special values interpolate in a new scalar domain.

Across the sine model, prime Euler factors, completed zeta, and finite-field zeta functions, the source repeatedly turns divisor geometry into reflection constraints. For completed Riemann zeta, the strongest one-vertical-line configuration compatible with reflection about the critical line is exactly RH; the finite-field discussion supplies a bounded multi-line analogue rather than a proof of the global case.

The source repeatedly separates divisor information from the extra data needed to make it effective: symmetric product organization and normalization permit coefficient extraction for sine, multiplication by exp(P) exposes divisor-preserving ambiguity, completion makes xi's relevant divisor and involutions visible, Poisson-Newton retains zero-supported correction terms beside the logarithmic-derivative transform, and gamma identities use divisor and order plus local or asymptotic normalization to remove residual freedom.

The source contrasts two mechanisms for zeta's functional equation: a Hankel contour whose residue lattice produces the reflected Dirichlet series, and theta self-reciprocity transported through a split Mellin transform. It then generalizes the Fourier-Mellin mechanism through adelic local-global duality and through modular forms, where Hecke eigenstructure separately supplies the Euler product.
